title: Compute Engine: machine families, custom types and what each one is for

videos.script: A machine type is the first thing you choose on Compute Engine. It is also the easiest thing to choose badly. This lesson is about choosing it well. {{lab}} First, the lab. Nothing in this course touches a Google Cloud account. Google publishes no imitation of its control plane. So you work with what runs on your own computer: gcloud, Terraform and Docker. {{sheet}} Every price comes from Google's public pages. You copy them into a short program once, and keep it. {{name}} Then the names. e2-standard-2 is three words. The series, the ratio, and the number of processors. {{families}} The family decides how much memory comes with each processor. That ratio decides most of the bill, and you will see what the wrong one costs in a year. {{custom}} Last, two exceptions. A custom type, priced from its parts. And a shared core, which sells you a quarter of a processor. Each is right in one place and expensive everywhere else.
